Configuring the NX-400 Edge Router for Fixed-Wireless Sites
DocumentKVT-DG-112RevisionC, 12 October 2026Applies toNX-400 hardware revision 2 and later, firmware 7.4.xOwnerAccess Network Engineering
1. Purpose and Scope

This guide describes how to install and configure an NX-400 edge router at a fixed-wireless base station. It covers the initial configuration, the VLAN plan, monitoring and the checks to complete before a site is handed over to operations. Changes to the core network are outside its scope and follow the change process in KVT-OPS-004.
2. Before You Start
Bring the following to site:
A laptop with an SSH client and the site configuration file from the provisioning portal.
The site's management IP address, gateway and VLAN identifiers.
A console cable (RJ45 to USB-C) and a spare SFP+ module.
A change ticket in the Approved state.
2.1 Safety
Never climb the tower or open the cabinet without a second person present. Report any damaged earth bonding before you begin work.
Warning. Do not connect the radio uplink until the router reports a valid configuration. An unconfigured router floods the backhaul with DHCP requests.

4. Initial Configuration
4.1 Load the base configuration
Connect to the console port at 115200 baud and log in with the factory account. Copy the site file to the router, check it with a dry run, then apply it:
scp KV-0417-base.yaml admin@192.0.2.1:/config/ ssh admin@192.0.2.1 nxcli config load /config/KV-0417-base.yaml --dry-run nxcli config load /config/KV-0417-base.yaml --commit --comment "KVT-CHG-30218"
The dry run must finish without errors before the commit is attempted.
4.2 Site configuration file
The site file is generated by the provisioning portal. A shortened example is shown below.

site: id: KV-0417 name: "Harrow Ridge" timezone: Europe/London management: vlan: 999 address: 10.41.7.2/29 gateway: 10.41.7.1 uplink: interface: xe-0/1/0 vlans: [100, 300] mtu: 9100 sectors: - { port: ge-0/0/0, vlan: 210, azimuth: 0 } - { port: ge-0/0/1, vlan: 211, azimuth: 120 } - { port: ge-0/0/2, vlan: 212, azimuth: 240 }

6. Monitoring
The router exports its metrics to the regional collector every 60 seconds. The telemetry section of the configuration must read as follows:
export = interfaces, optics, cpu, temperature
[telemetry] collector = 10.0.88.20:4317 interval _ s = 60 [alarms] optics _ rx _ low _ dbm = -18.0 temperature _ high _ c = 70
7. Acceptance Checks
Step 1 Confirm that all three sector ports are up and passing traffic.
Step 2 Run a 15-minute throughput test across the backhaul and record the result in the ticket.
Step 3 Check that the router appears on the monitoring dashboard with no active alarms.
Step 4 Photograph the cabinet, the cable labels and the earth bonding.
Step 5 Hand the site over to the Network Operations Centre by phone and close the ticket.
8. Troubleshooting

SymptomLikely causeActionSector port stays downRadio not powered, or PoE budget too lowCheck the injector LED and set the PoE budget to 30 W per portBackhaul drops every few minutesMTU mismatch with the far endSet the MTU to 9100 on both ends and reload the interfaceNo metrics on the dashboardCollector unreachable from VLAN 999Ping the collector from the router and raise a ticket with the NOC
If a fault cannot be cleared within two hours, roll back to the previous configuration and escalate to the oncall engineer.
